result.verdict: CONFIRMED_WITH_NOTES, 0 blocking under A115. This was a static review: nothing was run, and no run-tree path was opened, stat-ed or listed. Lenses 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 are confirmed; lens 4 is partial. (1) The main() bytes check is real. pinload reads eps_ngc91_c2v001.py once, checks 2e59a461 before compiling, and executes exactly those bytes. S1, S2, S3 and the timing wrappers leave every numeric path unchanged. (2) I recomputed the comparison in json-only Python. The rerun regenerates ce26ced9 byte for byte once its 90 seconds fields and the decisions block are restored. Against EPS_CERT_NGC91_V001 there are 0 differences over 15 keys x 89 shells. eps_max is 6.423015553962408e-4 at (2,3], CERTIFIED. (3) The GQ binding meets A132 D2(a). (4) Fence v003's exact entries equal root's pin paths only for IDENTITY and start; the fence carries no shas. The fence also allows reads that the producer guard (case-sensitive) refuses, so N2 is real. N3 does not breach root's read rules, but it is the realpath-before-refuse pattern that 0639 SA-CX1-B1 had removed from the seal path. (5) C1 holds and needs two extensions for S0. The V004 node maxima cannot be recomputed at a new point. The below-5 rule rests on the anchor's CHECK F1 evidence. (6) The timing and memory figures match the evidence and raw JSON. The post's 2.16x co-load attribution and its 1,070 s solo floor are incomplete. (7) The audit file is consistent with the conduct claims. UNTESTED under the hard rules: the V006 addendum quote (its path has an NGC3198 component), the TAIL_REANCHOR bytes and the be148bab bytes (both outside the allowed list), and External1's case sensitivity. Conduct disclosure: I wrote scratch scripts with heredoc cat and made one scratch mkdir -p without the taskpolicy -b prefix. Every program-tree read, hash and Python run used taskpolicy -b. The Python was stdlib only: json, hashlib, and ast to parse source text without running it. Progress lines are in claude_artifacts/review_ri45_06_c3/PARTIAL_lens.md (exclusive create, append only).

findings.title: Runner st3 loads the fence through SourceFileLoader after a separate sha read, and runs the producer through runpy with no sha check before it runs (0639 SA-CX1-B2 class). The main() bytes check itself is real.
findings.evidence: run_fenced_c4st3.py L13-20 checks FENCE.read_bytes() against 175b995b, then calls spec_from_file_location and exec_module. Under -I -B, sys.pycache_prefix is still None at that point (the producer sets it only later, at L151), so an existing build/tools/__pycache__/fence_c4v003.cpython-312.pyc would be used. L79-83 calls runpy.run_path(script) with no sha check. The producer's own sha 79a5ac1d is computed after the run, by re-reading __file__ (eps_ngc_point_c4v001.py L424). The chain is clean: pinload L144-166 reads each file once, checks the sha before compile, and compiles exactly that buffer; producer L227-229 checks that the chain bound to the verified modules. TESTED: no __pycache__ exists anywhere under ri45_06 (find -P), and 79a5ac1d equals the current bytes. Not reachable from honest pinned producers.
findings.label: FORMAL

findings.title: Fence v003 carries A132 D1(a) only in part. 'No other file in those trees' is enforced only by the case-sensitive producer guard (N2).
findings.evidence: fence_c4v003.py L37-41: PIN_IDENTITY and PIN_START equal the c0390172 paths (TESTED, string equality). There is no entry for A2_SEED_SCAN_G2 result.json and no sha in the fence. _forbidden_read (L92-109) has no rule for CLAUDE2/runs/, exempts .py files inside the NGC3198 run tree (L106), and has no UNT_INTERNAL_RUNS rule. The hook handles opens only, with no listdir or scandir check (L151-165), and skips fd opens (L152-154). An os.open with dir_fd is judged against the cwd. The guard (pinload L79-91) matches '/CLAUDE2/runs/', '/CLAUDE2/runs_ext', 'UNT_INTERNAL_RUNS' and 'ROOT_DECISIONS_' case-sensitively. So on the case-insensitive internal volume, '/CLAUDE2/RUNS/<non-NGC3198 run>/...', case-variant .py paths in the NGC3198 run, and 'unt_internal_runs' pass both layers. A case-variant External1 spelling of CLAUDE2/runs_ext would pass both if External1 is case-insensitive (UNTESTED). The actual reads conformed (FORMAL, from the guard logs): run-tree opens only at the 3 pins, read-only, given path equal to resolved path, 0 refusals, 0 run-tree listings. Honest producers use canonical literals (lwr_common L18-20, certs_common L24-42). No read rule in 0677 or 0685 is breached; the instruction 'add them as exact entries in your fence v003' is met only in part.
findings.label: FORMAL

findings.title: N3: the fence hook (and the guard) resolve realpath before refusing, on every open. The selftest's runs_ext trial calls lstat and readlink on the link and lstat on its External1 target.
findings.evidence: fence _hook L155-157 computes os.path.realpath(lit) before _forbidden_read tests lit against RUNS_EXT (L93). The selftest's 'read_runs_ext' trial (L181) therefore calls lstat and readlink on CLAUDE2/runs_ext, lstats the External1 target chain, and looks up the absent probe name. pinload _guard L105-107 uses the same order. Root's rules are read rules (0677; 0685 D1(a); 0506/0507/0509 on C5H and runs_ext/UVT_*). Nothing under runs_ext was opened, listed or read, and C5H was not touched, so there is no breach. But 0639 SA-CX1-B1 had this same pattern removed from the seal path, and Claude4 disclosed it before (0092 HARNESS-N1, 0149 P-N1); it is still in v003. In 0178, 'Nothing existed' is true only of the probe names: the link and its target directory exist and were lstat-ed.
findings.label: FORMAL

findings.title: C1 is confirmed. The wrong 'lo < 5' scope persists in the exclusive-create POINT_NOTE copies, and the V004 node maxima cannot be recomputed at a new point.
findings.evidence: eps_ngc91_c2v001.py L79-97: node maxima (from EPS_CERT_K128_V004) and the check's own sup (EPS_SUP_SUPP) enter actual_vals on every shell where they are present. From there they reach eps_actual_set, eps for lo<5 (L88), eps = max(envelope, actual) for lo>=5 (L86), envelope_over_actual (L91) and envelope_dominates_actual (L97). The anchor values are also stored in the eps_check_own_sup and eps_node_maxima_from_V004 fields. Every such value is below the local max (closest ratios: 0.999999921 on (4,5] and 0.999999409 on (12,13]), and dropping them leaves all 89 eps values unchanged at the anchor. The node maxima are |1-q| of stored anchor-state responses (eps_cert_c2v004 node_shell_eps L43-54: U0, S0 and dk from the T120L stored operator and the DDO C4R3 cache). So 'recompute them at the point' (POINT_NOTE; the Next section of 0178) is not available at S0 thetas.

findings.title: The timing figures match. The '2.16x, from co-load' attribution and the '~1,070 s solo' planning floor are incomplete.
findings.evidence: evidence.timing equals raw.timing (80677579). Total 2,314.604 = 3.385 + 2,311.16 + 0.059. The main() parts sum to within 0.001 s. Per shell: wall 5.643-74.369 s, CPU 5.565-11.653 s, with the CPU max at (2,3]. The CPU alone, 1,209.86 s, exceeds the record's main() wall of 1,068.5 s, and the shells' CPU of 667.82 s is 1.22x the record shell sum of 546.38 s. raw ri_runnable_time is 2,378.7 s, about the wall: the process was runnable throughout and got CPU about 52% of the time. The absolute nice was 15: the first ps sample shows NI 5 before nice -n 10. top showed 0.1% CPU at 10:30:49Z. The record ran with up to 3 concurrent processes at nice 10 and default QoS. So the post's 'solo' 1,070 s is not a planning floor for the background-QoS S0 runs (0689), for which no solo figure was measured. The evidence JSON's own 'not like-for-like' caveat is correct.
findings.label: TESTED
